learning_outcomes.text: Students name management tasks in industrial practice and classify behavioral science aspects of management as well as concepts of organizational structure, human resource management, and business administration within them.
They know various scientific approaches to the sustainability discussion as well as technical rules for implementing sustainability in the engineering profession.
Students integrate the methods of business organization in the design of various management systems.
They have detailed knowledge of sustainability assessment and can select processes for emission and resource avoidance and design selected procedures.
Students evaluate methodical concepts of system design in relation to the requirement levels of technical management.

They can specifically develop sustainable development projects for a company in the areas of climate and resource protection and place their technical expertise in the context of the sustainability debate.
Students can apply the learned methods of management and sustainability assessment to concrete problems.

For example, they adapt basic methods of Lean Management to design organizational and process structures, apply simple investment appraisal and cost accounting procedures, or use standard software for concrete carbon footprint analysis of process chains.
Students take into account different perspectives and interests of other stakeholders when solving tasks related to corporate organization and sustainability assessment.
They can structuredly present and deliver results developed in groups.

Students justify the necessity of organizational control and the consideration of sustainability aspects in industrial practice and reflect on their own responsibility both as an employee and as a consumer.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to corporate organization and management
Assessment of sustainability in the engineering sector
assessment_rules: The portfolio examination consists of a presentation and two e-exams, totaling 100 points. The presentation accounts for a maximum of 20 points. There are three e-exam opportunities, each evaluated with a maximum of 40 points. Students can participate in all three e-exams, and the two e-exams with the best results will be included in the final evaluation.
